page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 12 dedicated physical cores with 12 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 core-to-thread mapping. The memory allocation is 96.0 GB of RAM, which translates to 8.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by the stress-ng multi-core score of 8837.03 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4693.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average throughput, reaching 59.2 GB/sec for uncached large block reads, though the Passmark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, this server is configured for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. It is suitable for database operations, as reflected by its average Passmark database score and Redis SET performance of 8.48 million operations per second. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which, combined with the 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth, makes it less suitable for high-throughput static web serving. The hardware profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that benefit from dedicated physical cores but can tolerate moderate CPU clock speeds.
